body.working_title: Software and services for arranging music into notated scores for chosen instruments (2026)

body.name: Ivan Svetunkov
body.words: 1. Ivan Svetunkov, you know my ORCID. 2. git@github.com:Syntonic-Labs/research.git repo 3. The name is fine 4. Yes, research prototypes count. Keep the hypothesis

body.text: Before this record was opened, in the same chat on 2026-11-19 (17:48-17:57 UTC), the agent ran five unrecorded web searches (AI auto arranger software; automatic arrangement MIDI plugins; Band-in-a-Box 2026; MusicXML automatic arrangement for chosen instruments; Sibelius Arrange feature) and told the supervisor it found no commercial product that takes a MusicXML score and arranges it live for chosen instruments. Products seen then: Band-in-a-Box, RapidComposer, JMT Orchestrator, BackupBand, Texturium, Orb Composer, LANDR Composer, InstaComposer, Muse, ShevtoneAudio, Sibelius Arrange, Dorico Explode, Klangio, Songscription, AiHud Notation Copilot, and research systems (NeurIPS 2025 unified arrangement model; CMMR 2023 monophonic MusicXML arranger). That exploration suggested hypothesis H1 and is not evidence for it.

As of November 2026, which software products, online services and research systems can automatically or semi-automatically arrange existing music into a notated score that musicians read, for a set of instruments the user chooses; and for each, what input it takes, what notation it outputs, whether it uses machine learning or rules, and whether it works interactively or in real time?

body.definition: A software product, online service or research system that, from existing musical material (a melody, chords, a score or a performance), automatically or semi-automatically produces parts for instruments: by orchestrating, harmonising, voicing, exploding or reducing. The unit of analysis: one system, counted once across versions and editions.

The system delivers its arrangement as notation a musician reads: a score or parts in standard staff notation, exported as MusicXML, PDF or a notation application's file, or written into a notation editor.

code.include: The system's own description or documentation shows the arrangement as staff notation, or exports MusicXML, PDF score/parts, or a notation-app file.
code.exclude: Output only as audio, MIDI without notation, tablature or chord charts alone, or piano-roll.

body.definition: The user selects the instruments or ensemble the arrangement is written for.

code.include: The user picks target instruments, an ensemble, or a template of instruments, and the parts are written for that choice.
code.exclude: A fixed instrumentation (e.g. piano only, or a style's fixed band) the user cannot change instrument by instrument.

body.definition: The system accepts notated music as its input.

code.include: Accepts MusicXML, or works on a score inside a notation application (which reads MusicXML).
code.exclude: Accepts only audio, MIDI, chord symbols, text prompts or live playing.

body.definition: The arrangement is produced by a model trained on data (machine learning, neural network, LLM).

code.include: The developer states that a trained model (machine learning, neural network, deep learning, LLM, 'AI model') generates the arrangement.
code.exclude: 'AI' used as a label without saying that a trained model produces the arrangement; such systems are coded unclear method.

body.definition: The arrangement is produced by hand-written rules, styles, templates or algorithms without a trained model.

code.include: The developer describes style files, templates, rules, voice-leading algorithms or search procedures, or an independent review does.
code.exclude: Any trained model generating the arrangement.

body.definition: The sources do not say whether a trained model or rules produce the arrangement.

code.include: Marketed as 'AI' or 'intelligent' with no statement of how the arrangement is produced.
code.exclude: Either ML method or rules method applies.

body.definition: The arrangement is regenerated in response to the user's choices or playing without an offline export-import cycle.

code.include: Arrangement updates live as the user plays, changes instruments or settings, within the same session.
code.exclude: A one-off batch generation the user must re-run from scratch.

body.definition: Sold or licensed to the public (paid, subscription or freemium) at the date of retrieval.

code.include: A price, subscription or purchase page exists at retrieval.
code.exclude: Free open-source, free-only, discontinued, or research-only systems.

body.definition: Available to the public at no cost at retrieval.

code.include: Free download or free web use, or published code.
code.exclude: Paid-only or research descriptions without public access.

body.definition: Described in a research publication (paper, preprint, thesis) rather than offered as a product.

code.include: The source is a paper, preprint or thesis describing the system.
code.exclude: A product whose maker also published a paper is coded by its availability as a product.

body.definition: A commercially available arranging system, not made by Syntonic Labs, that takes score input and uses an ML method to produce notated output for a user-chosen instrumentation.

code.include: The same system is coded commercially available, score input, ML method, notated output and user-chosen instrumentation.
code.exclude: Any of the five missing, or the system is a Syntonic Labs product (Tempered).

body.definition: A fixed set of web searches run on one or two days, each result screened against the inclusion criteria, with one level of snowballing from included roundups, then each included system coded by a fixed codebook (summative content analysis, deductive).

body.statement: No [[TM9:commercially available]] [[TM1:arranging system]] made by others than Syntonic Labs is a [[TM12:full-match arranger]]: none takes [[TM4:score input]] and uses an [[TM5:ML method]] to produce [[TM2:notated output]] for a [[TM3:user-chosen instrumentation]].

body.design: Market scan (TM13): run the 20 fixed queries in claimset-code/score-arrangers-2026/queries.txt once each (WebSearch, standard mode; 15 general and research queries, 5 aimed at Reddit, KVR, MuseScore and Gearspace forums), screen every result against the inclusion criteria, snowball one level from included roundups and forum threads, build one dossier per included system from its own pages (product page, pricing page, documentation, paper), capture it, and code it with the codebook TM2-TM12 and TM14-TM23 (pass 1, this agent). A second agent, registered before it starts and working in its own log, independently codes (pass 2) a 25% random sample of the dossiers (Python random.sample, seed 2026, over dossier IDs in capture order). Syntonic Labs products and human arranging services are excluded.
body.analysis: Count pass-1 dossiers coded full-match arranger (TM12), and dossiers coded all five of commercially available, score input, ML method, notated output and user-chosen instrumentation; the two counts check each other. The verdict is computed by the tool's count over pass 1.
body.new_data: The pre-record searches (NT1) were five ad-hoc queries; this test uses a fixed set of 20 queries and snowballing, a frame fixed before any of it is run, and codes each system against written criteria. Systems seen in NT1 are likely to reappear: the test is new in its frame and coding, not wholly in its material.

body.definition: Sold for a single payment (a perpetual licence), possibly with paid upgrades.

code.include: A one-off price or perpetual licence is listed at retrieval.
code.exclude: Subscription-only or free.

body.definition: Paid by recurring fee (monthly or yearly), or by credits bought repeatedly.

code.include: A monthly or yearly price, or credit packs, listed at retrieval.
code.exclude: One-off purchase only, or free.

body.definition: A free version or free use exists alongside paid options (freemium), or the system is wholly free.

code.include: Free plan, free version, free trial longer than a demo, or wholly free use.
code.exclude: Time-limited trial of a paid product only, or no public access.

body.definition: No price could be found in the dossier.

code.include: The dossier shows no price or pricing model.
code.exclude: Any price or pricing model stated.

body.definition: Runs as a standalone application on a computer.

code.include: Downloadable standalone program for Windows, macOS or Linux.
code.exclude: Runs only inside another host (plugin) or in a browser.

body.definition: Used in a web browser or through an online API.

code.include: Browser-based app or online API.
code.exclude: Desktop-only or plugin-only.

body.definition: Runs inside a digital audio workstation (VST, AU, AAX, MIDI effect).

code.include: Offered in a DAW plugin format.
code.exclude: Notation-app plugins; standalone apps only.

body.definition: Runs inside a notation application (Sibelius, Dorico, MuseScore, Finale) as a plugin or built-in feature.

code.include: A notation application's own feature, or a plugin for one.
code.exclude: Exports to a notation app without running inside it.

body.definition: Runs as an app on a phone or tablet.

code.include: iOS, iPadOS or Android app.
code.exclude: Mobile web only (coded web service).

body.definition: Available only as source code, a library or model weights, with no packaged application.

code.include: Published code, library or weights only.
code.exclude: Any packaged application, plugin or web service.

body.analysis: Run 1: claimset-code/score-arrangers-2026/tally.py counts pass-1 systems: in total; with each code; by method and availability; by platform and method; by pricing and method; and, among systems with notated output for a user-chosen instrumentation, by input (score or other) and method; it also counts systems without exactly one method or availability code, as a check. include: An arranging system (TM1): software product, online service or research system that automatically or semi-automatically produces instrumental parts from existing musical material

Public information about it is available at retrieval (product page, documentation, paper or forum account)
exclude: Human arranging services (people hired to arrange)
Audio-only generators that output finished audio with no parts (e.g. text-to-song)
Pure transcription (audio to notation of the same parts) with no arranging
Notation editors and DAWs without an arranging function
Generators of a single line only (melody, chord progression or drum loop) with no arrangement across instruments
Pages that name no system (general articles), except roundups and threads, which are used for snowballing

body.text: The shell cannot reach the web (the session's proxy refuses product sites, KVR and arXiv), so pages are read with the WebFetch tool, which returns a model's rendering of the page rather than a byte copy. Each dossier is captured as that returned text, with the URLs and retrieval times, and says so in its description. Codings therefore code whole dossiers and quote no excerpts, since a quote must come from the page itself. Search result lists are saved as returned by WebSearch.
